questions.passage: Traditionally, certain features of mosque architecture are nearly [vocab]______[/vocab], such as the mihrab (or niche), which almost all mosques include. But mosques can also be built to reflect a multitude of different architectural styles, as in the case of the Great Mosque of Central Java, which includes elements from the Javanese and Greek revival styles.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: universal

choices.label: B
choices.text: elaborate

choices.label: C
choices.text: illusory

choices.label: D
choices.text: idealized

explanation.key_evidence: The passage says the mihrab is a feature "which almost all mosques include."
explanation.why_correct: Because the mihrab appears in almost all mosques, the blank needs a word meaning widely present. "Universal" best conveys that idea, while the second sentence contrasts this common feature with the many styles mosques can have.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. "Universal" means found nearly everywhere or shared broadly, matching "almost all mosques include."
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. "Elaborate" means complex or detailed, but the passage is about how common the feature is, not how ornate it is.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. "Illusory" means deceptive or unreal, which does not fit a real architectural feature.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. "Idealized" suggests representing a perfect form, but the sentence is about prevalence.

explanation.short: The mihrab is described as something almost all mosques include, so the feature is nearly universal.
explanation.detailed: The passage says the mihrab is a feature "which almost all mosques include." Because the blank describes how common certain mosque features are, "universal" is the most precise completion. The following sentence then contrasts this commonality with the variety of architectural styles mosques can reflect.

questions.passage: The dates that archaeologists assign to most of the colossal sculptures of human heads produced by the Olmec civilization of Mesoamerica are necessarily [vocab]______[/vocab]. The majority of the sculptures have been moved from their original context, making precise dating impossible.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: uncontroversial

choices.label: B
choices.text: irrelevant

choices.label: C
choices.text: applicable

choices.label: D
choices.text: approximate

explanation.key_evidence: The passage says the sculptures have been moved from their original context, "making precise dating impossible."
explanation.why_correct: If precise dating is impossible, the dates archaeologists assign cannot be exact. They must therefore be approximate.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. The passage does not discuss whether the dates are controversial.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. The dates still matter; the problem is that they cannot be exact.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. "Applicable" does not express the idea of inexact dating.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. "Approximate" means close but not exact, which follows directly from the impossibility of precise dating.

explanation.short: Because precise dating is impossible, the dates must be approximate.
explanation.detailed: The passage explains that most sculptures were moved from their original context, "making precise dating impossible." That means archaeologists can still estimate dates, but those dates cannot be exact. "Approximate" is therefore the logical completion.

questions.passage: [vocab]______[/vocab] traditional descriptions of pollination syndromes (suites of floral traits, such as nectar composition and symmetry, hypothesized to have independently evolved as a result of selection pressure exerted by pollinators) and recent empirical observations of floral-trait combinations have led some ecologists to express reservations about the utility of those descriptions.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Discrepancies between

choices.label: B
choices.text: Proclamations of

choices.label: C
choices.text: Recurrences of

choices.label: D
choices.text: Affinities between

explanation.key_evidence: Ecologists have "reservations about the utility" of traditional descriptions after comparing them with recent observations.
explanation.why_correct: Reservations would naturally arise if traditional pollination-syndrome descriptions do not match recent empirical observations. "Discrepancies between" names that mismatch.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. "Discrepancies between" means differences or mismatches, which explains why ecologists would question the descriptions.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. "Proclamations of" would mean announcements, which does not create a logical reason for doubt.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. "Recurrences of" means repeated instances, not conflict between descriptions and observations.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. "Affinities between" means similarities or connections, the opposite of the mismatch needed here.

explanation.short: The sentence needs a phrase that explains why ecologists doubt the traditional descriptions: mismatches between those descriptions and observations.
explanation.detailed: The passage says traditional descriptions and recent observations have led ecologists to question the utility of those descriptions. Such doubts make sense if the two do not align. "Discrepancies between" precisely expresses that conflict.

questions.passage: The following text is from Louise Erdrich's 1986 novel The Beet Queen. The narrator discusses her relationship with her young niece, Dot. Celestine, the narrator's sister-in-law, is Dot's mother. Dot and I had a mental connection, I was sure of it. I understood things about the baby that her mother could not accept. For instance, she was never meant to be a baby. Dot was as impatient with babyhood as I. She tried at once to grow out of it. Celestine never saw that, because she, and only she, took pleasure in Dot's helpless softness. Only Celestine was saddened by her daughter's fierce progress. Day by day, Dot grew stronger. In her shopping-cart stroller she exercised to exhaustion, bouncing for hours to develop her leg muscles. ©1986 by Louise Erdrich
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To present the narrator's belief that she understands Dot better than Celestine does

choices.label: B
choices.text: To speculate that when Dot is older, her personality will be like Celestine's

choices.label: C
choices.text: To discuss what the narrator and Celestine do to amuse Dot

choices.label: D
choices.text: To compare the narrator's physical appearance to the physical appearance of Celestine

explanation.key_evidence: The narrator says, "I understood things about the baby that her mother could not accept," and later says Celestine "never saw" Dot’s impatience with babyhood.
explanation.why_correct: The text centers on the narrator’s belief that she sees Dot’s nature more clearly than Celestine does. Details about Dot’s impatience and Celestine’s attachment to Dot’s babyhood support that contrast.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. The passage presents the narrator’s belief that she understands Dot better than Celestine does.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. The passage does not predict that Dot will grow up to resemble Celestine.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. The focus is not on amusing Dot.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. The passage does not compare the narrator’s and Celestine’s appearances.

explanation.short: The passage mainly presents the narrator’s belief that she understands Dot better than Celestine does.
explanation.detailed: From the opening claim that the narrator and Dot have a "mental connection," the passage contrasts the narrator’s view of Dot with Celestine’s. The narrator believes Dot is eager to move beyond babyhood, while Celestine enjoys Dot’s helplessness. That makes choice A the best description of the text’s purpose.

questions.passage: Adelaide is one of many cities that have installed pontoons or other hardening structures to protect their shorelines against coastal hazards. To assess how birds respond to shoreline hardening and other landscape alterations, Diann Prosser et al. used a tool known as the Index of Waterbird Community Integrity to survey bird communities consisting of sixty-four species, including the tundra swan and the great blue heron, in the Chesapeake Bay on the US East Coast. The researchers concluded that shoreline hardening more negatively affects birds than does land development for uses such as housing.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It introduces a certain technique, mentions the hypothesis of a study into an ecological consequence of that technique, and presents evidence in support of that study's hypothesis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It provides an example of a location that has adopted a particular approach, explains the methodology of a study into an ecological effect of that approach, and describes a finding of that study.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It makes a claim about the use of a specific strategy, describes field observations of a consequence of that strategy in a particular ecosystem, and makes a supposition based on those observations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It presents a solution to a commonly occurring problem, summarizes the procedures used by a group of researchers studying the environmental impact of that solution, and notes the significance of the researchers' findings.

explanation.short: The passage moves from a location example to a study method and then to the study's conclusion.
explanation.key_evidence: Adelaide used shoreline hardening; Prosser's team used an index to survey birds; the researchers concluded hardening was more harmful.
explanation.why_correct: B follows the text's sequence: an adopted approach in one location, a method for studying an ecological effect, and the resulting finding.
explanation.detailed: Classify each sentence by what it does. The first gives an example of shoreline protection, the second describes a bird-community survey, and the third reports the comparative conclusion. The text does not separately explain the broader significance or implications of that conclusion.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. The study's last sentence is its finding, not a hypothesis followed by separate supporting evidence.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. Example, methodology, and finding appear in precisely that order.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. The passage identifies a formal survey method and reports its conclusion, rather than ending with an unsupported supposition.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. The last sentence states what the researchers found; it does not go on to discuss the significance of their finding.

questions.passage: Women like Dorothy T. Blum made important early contributions to the history of US cryptology, a field concerned with secure data communication and storage. Blum provided cryptological services for the US Army in the 1940s and then joined the National Security Agency (NSA). She was a pioneer in transitioning the NSA to using computers for cryptoanalysis. In this way, Blum and others like her helped make it possible for more women—such as Maureen Baginski, who currently works in intelligence and supports the FBI—to enter the field of cryptology.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cryptology is a field that focuses primarily on securely managing data.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Women such as Dorothy T. Blum and Maureen Baginski have contributed to the field of cryptology.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dorothy T. Blum and Maureen Baginski worked together on an important project in the field of cryptology.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cryptology should be taught more often in schools to encourage more women to enter the field.

explanation.key_evidence: The passage says women like Dorothy T. Blum made early contributions to US cryptology and that Blum helped make it possible for more women, such as Maureen Baginski, to enter the field.
explanation.why_correct: The passage uses Blum and Baginski as examples to support the broader idea that women have contributed to cryptology over time.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. It defines cryptology, but that detail is too narrow to be the main idea.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. It captures the passage’s central focus on women’s contributions to cryptology.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. The passage never says Blum and Baginski worked together.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. The passage does not argue that cryptology should be taught more often in schools.

explanation.short: The main idea is that women such as Blum and Baginski have contributed to cryptology.
explanation.detailed: The opening sentence states that women like Dorothy T. Blum made important early contributions to US cryptology. The passage then explains Blum’s work and connects it to later women in the field, including Maureen Baginski. Choice B best captures this central point.

questions.passage: Researchers who examined data from radio-tagged southern sea otters (Enhydra lutris nereis) identified fitness benefits gained by otters that used tools. By using fixed stones as anvils, tool-using otters gained access to high-quality, hard-shelled prey (e.g., mussels and clams) that they could usually not access through biting alone. Non-tool-using otters foraged abundant, energy-poor, easily extractable prey instead (e.g., snails). Even when easily processed prey were depleted, tool-using otters that processed mussels and clams were thus able to obtain their needed energy resources and to do so without incurring tooth damage.
questions.prompt: What does the text most strongly suggest about southern sea otters in environments where snails, mussels, and clams are present?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Those otters whose diet consists mainly of snails will likely exhibit less tooth damage than will those otters that use tools to consume mussels and clams.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Those otters that do not use tools will likely have more robust health than those otters that do use tools.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Those otters that do not use tools will likely need to process larger amounts of prey to meet their energy requirements than will those otters that use tools.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Those otters that consume mussels and clams without the use of tools will likely spend less time foraging than will those otters that use tools to access the same prey resources.

explanation.key_evidence: Non-tool-using otters forage "energy-poor" prey, while tool-using otters gain access to "high-quality, hard-shelled prey."
explanation.why_correct: If non-tool-using otters rely on lower-energy prey, they would likely need more prey items to meet the same energy needs than otters that can access higher-quality prey with tools.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. The passage says tool use helps otters avoid tooth damage when processing hard-shelled prey; it does not suggest snail-eating otters have less tooth damage than tool users.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. The passage identifies fitness benefits for tool-using otters, not better health for non-tool users.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. It follows from the contrast between energy-poor prey and high-quality prey.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. The passage does not support a claim about shorter foraging time for otters eating mussels and clams without tools.

explanation.short: Because non-tool-using otters eat lower-energy prey, they would likely need to process more prey to get enough energy.
explanation.detailed: The passage contrasts non-tool-using otters, which forage abundant but "energy-poor" prey, with tool-using otters, which can access high-quality mussels and clams. Since each low-energy prey item provides less energy, non-tool users would likely need larger quantities to meet their energy requirements.

questions.passage: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz is a 1900 novel by L. Frank Baum. In the novel, Dorothy lives in Kansas with her aunt and uncle, but she later finds herself in a land called Oz. The narrator indicates that her aunt and uncle’s house in Kansas is remote and solitary, writing that ______
questions.prompt: Which quotation from The Wonderful Wizard of Oz most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: in Oz, “[Dorothy and her companions] passed through the rest of the forest in safety, and when they came out from its gloom saw before them a steep hill, covered from top to bottom with great pieces of rock.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: in Oz, “Dorothy fell asleep only once, and then she dreamed she was in Kansas, where Aunt Em was telling her how glad she was to have her little girl at home again.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: in Kansas, “Dorothy lived in the midst of the great Kansas prairies, with Uncle Henry, who was a farmer, and Aunt Em, who was the farmer’s wife.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: in Kansas, “When Dorothy stood in the doorway and looked around, she could see nothing but the great gray prairie on every side. Not a tree nor a house broke the broad sweep of flat country.”

explanation.key_evidence: Choice D says Dorothy could see "nothing but the great gray prairie" and that "not a tree nor a house" broke the flat country.
explanation.why_correct: The claim is that the Kansas house is remote and solitary. A view with no trees or houses in any direction directly illustrates isolation.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. It describes a scene in Oz, not the Kansas house.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. It mentions Kansas in a dream but does not describe the house as remote or solitary.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. It identifies Dorothy’s household but does not show isolation.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. It directly depicts the house as surrounded by empty prairie with no nearby trees or houses.

explanation.short: Choice D best illustrates a remote, solitary house because it describes empty prairie with no trees or other houses nearby.
explanation.detailed: The prompt asks for a quotation showing that Dorothy’s Kansas house is remote and solitary. Choice D provides exactly that image: Dorothy sees only prairie on every side, with no tree or house interrupting the landscape. This directly supports the claim.

questions.passage: Carcinization, or the evolution of a crablike body form, has taken place in crustaceans many times over the last 250 million years. Decarcinization has occurred several times as well, even though it involves the loss of traits such as sideways walking that seem to have helped carcinized groups persist in a variety of ecosystems. In a 2021 paper, Joanna Wolfe and team note that many decarcinized groups are extinct and have very few living relatives—signs that decarcinization might be an "evolutionary dead-end." But the team also discusses frog crabs, a living decarcinized group with traits suited to dwelling in sediment; fossils show that the group had decarcinized members as far back as the Early Cretaceous. This example suggests that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the evolutionary benefits of a crablike body form are less certain than many studies of carcinization had previously implied.

choices.label: B
choices.text: despite having many living relatives, some decarcinized groups did not benefit from decarcinization.

choices.label: C
choices.text: sideways walking may have been less important to the survival of frog crabs than a protected abdomen and other traits associated with carcinization.

choices.label: D
choices.text: a crablike body form may not be optimal in all cases, with ecological conditions sometimes favoring the persistence of decarcinization.

explanation.key_evidence: The passage says frog crabs are a living decarcinized group with traits suited to dwelling in sediment, even though many decarcinized groups appear to be evolutionary dead ends.
explanation.why_correct: The frog crab example qualifies the earlier claim. It suggests that although decarcinization is often unsuccessful, some environments can favor decarcinized forms, so a crablike body form is not always best.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. The passage does not broadly reject the benefits of a crablike body form; it complicates the idea that the crablike form is always optimal.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. The passage says many decarcinized groups have few living relatives, and it does not claim frog crabs failed to benefit from decarcinization.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. This focuses on particular traits but does not complete the broader conclusion about ecological conditions.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. It draws the supported conclusion that ecological conditions can sometimes favor decarcinized forms.

explanation.short: The frog crab example shows that decarcinization can persist when ecological conditions favor it.
explanation.detailed: The passage first presents evidence that decarcinization may often be an evolutionary dead end. It then introduces frog crabs as a living decarcinized group with sediment-dwelling traits and a long fossil history. That example supports the broader conclusion in choice D: a crablike body form may not be optimal in every ecological context.

questions.passage: A group of primate conservationists recently began a long-term study of the effects of different conservation strategies on the northern muriqui (Brachyteles hypoxanthus). The species population is currently estimated to be around 1,000. It is challenging to accurately count these primates, however, which makes it difficult to tell whether the population is increasing, decreasing, or staying stable. The study may thus ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: cause other conservationists to adopt a new methodology for counting populations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: risk making inaccurate conclusions about the effectiveness of different conservation strategies.

choices.label: C
choices.text: benefit from including species beyond the northern muriqui.

choices.label: D
choices.text: fail to consider less-well-known conservation approaches for the northern muriqui.

explanation.key_evidence: The passage says it is difficult to count northern muriquis accurately, making it hard to know whether the population is increasing, decreasing, or stable.
explanation.why_correct: A study of conservation strategies depends on measuring population changes. If those changes cannot be measured accurately, the study may draw inaccurate conclusions about which strategies work.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. The passage does not suggest the study will create a new counting method for other conservationists.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. The counting difficulty directly threatens the accuracy of conclusions about strategy effectiveness.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. The issue is not that the study includes too few species; it is that this species is hard to count.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. The passage does not say the study ignores any conservation approaches.

explanation.short: Because the population is hard to count accurately, the study may misjudge how effective the conservation strategies are.
explanation.detailed: The study aims to evaluate different conservation strategies for the northern muriqui. But the passage says the animals are difficult to count, which makes population trends uncertain. Without reliable trend data, the study risks drawing inaccurate conclusions about whether the strategies are working.

questions.passage: Mountain goats were made to climb. In addition to having hard hooves that can dig into nearly any groove or _____ mountain goats have slender bodies ideal for scaling nearly ninety-degree cliffs.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: crack, or

choices.label: B
choices.text: crack or

choices.label: C
choices.text: crack

choices.label: D
choices.text: crack,

explanation.key_evidence: The sentence begins with the introductory phrase "In addition to having hard hooves that can dig into nearly any groove or crack."
explanation.why_correct: That introductory phrase must be separated from the main clause "mountain goats have slender bodies" with a comma. Choice D preserves the phrase "groove or crack" and places the comma after "crack."

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. "crack, or mountain goats" incorrectly treats the main clause as part of an "or" pair.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. It omits the comma needed after the long introductory phrase.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. It also omits the needed comma before the main clause.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. It keeps "groove or crack" together and adds the required comma after the introductory phrase.

explanation.short: The introductory phrase must end with a comma before the main clause begins.
explanation.detailed: The sentence starts with a long introductory phrase: "In addition to having hard hooves that can dig into nearly any groove or crack." Standard English places a comma after that phrase before the main clause, "mountain goats have slender bodies." Choice D supplies exactly that comma.

questions.passage: As an object-oriented computer programming language, Perl is used by coders like Black Girls Code founder Kimberly Bryant to create computer programs by manipulating "objects" (that is, specifically defined variables or combinations of variables) into interacting with each other. Conversely, languages like Scheme, used in software development, ______ object oriented.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: is not

choices.label: B
choices.text: are not

choices.label: C
choices.text: was not

choices.label: D
choices.text: has not been

explanation.key_evidence: The subject of the blank is the plural noun "languages" in "languages like Scheme."
explanation.why_correct: Because the subject is plural and the sentence is in the present tense, the verb must be "are not."

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. "is" does not agree with the plural subject "languages."
choice_analysis.B: Correct. "Are not" agrees with the plural subject and fits the present-tense contrast.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. "Was" is singular and past tense.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. "Has" is singular and creates an incorrect verb phrase here.

explanation.short: The plural subject "languages" requires the plural verb phrase "are not."
explanation.detailed: The sentence contrasts Perl with "languages like Scheme." Since "languages" is plural, the verb must also be plural. Choice B, "are not," correctly completes the sentence.

questions.passage: In premodern Europe, one could sail from the east coast of England to the Netherlands or France faster than one could travel by land to England's capital, London. In that era, historian Michael Pye argues in his 2015 book The Edge of the World: A Cultural History of the North Sea and the Transformation of Europe, the North Sea did more to link the various peoples, cultures, and economies on _____ shores than to divide them.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: it's

choices.label: B
choices.text: its

choices.label: C
choices.text: their

choices.label: D
choices.text: they're

explanation.key_evidence: The sentence refers to the North Sea and then to the peoples, cultures, and economies on its shores.
explanation.why_correct: The blank needs the possessive form of the singular pronoun "it" to show that the shores belong to or border the North Sea. "Its" is the correct possessive form.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. "It’s" means "it is," which does not show possession.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. "Its" is the possessive form needed before "shores."
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. "Their" is plural and does not agree with the singular North Sea.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. "They’re" means "they are," which is not possessive.

explanation.short: The sentence needs the possessive pronoun "its" to refer to the North Sea’s shores.
explanation.detailed: The blank comes before "shores," so it must show possession. Because the North Sea is singular, the correct possessive pronoun is "its," not "it’s" or a plural form.

questions.passage: Creating personas—brief profiles of imaginary characters that represent key segments of a customer base—can help user experience (UX) designers think like and empathize with those using their products. Fictional yet realistic, ______
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: these personas include specific details (demographics, browsing habits, etc.) that UX designers draw from actual users.

choices.label: B
choices.text: specific details that UX designers draw from actual users (demographics, browsing habits, etc.) are included in these personas.

choices.label: C
choices.text: UX designers include specific details (demographics, browsing habits, etc.) drawn from actual users in these personas.

choices.label: D
choices.text: actual users are the source of the specific details (demographics, browsing habits, etc.) that UX designers include in these personas.

explanation.key_evidence: The modifier "Fictional yet realistic" describes the personas introduced in the previous sentence.
explanation.why_correct: A modifier at the beginning of a sentence should logically describe the subject that follows it. Choice A begins the main clause with "these personas," so the modifier attaches clearly and correctly.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. "These personas" is the noun being described as fictional yet realistic.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. It makes "specific details" the subject, but details are not what are fictional yet realistic.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. It makes UX designers the subject, creating a misplaced modifier.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. It makes actual users the subject, also creating a misplaced modifier.

explanation.short: The opening modifier must describe personas, and choice A makes "these personas" the subject.
explanation.detailed: The phrase "Fictional yet realistic" refers to the personas, not to details, designers, or users. Choice A correctly places "these personas" immediately after the modifier, avoiding a dangling or misplaced modifier.

questions.passage: In February 1864, James Johnson joined the US Army. He went on to serve in the 18th New York Cavalry during the US Civil War and, _____ earned a place in US history as one of the war's few Chinese-born American soldiers.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: usually,

choices.label: B
choices.text: for instance,

choices.label: C
choices.text: in any case,

choices.label: D
choices.text: in doing so,

explanation.key_evidence: Johnson served in the 18th New York Cavalry and, as a result, earned a place in US history.
explanation.why_correct: "In doing so" means "by doing that." It connects Johnson’s service with the result that he became one of the few Chinese-born American soldiers in the Civil War.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. "Usually" suggests frequency, which is not the relationship between the ideas.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. "For instance" introduces an example, but the second clause is a result, not an example.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. "In any case" suggests a shift or dismissal, not a cause-and-result relationship.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. "In doing so" shows that by serving, Johnson earned his place in history.

explanation.short: "In doing so" correctly shows that Johnson earned his place in history by serving.
explanation.detailed: The sentence says Johnson joined the Army and served in the 18th New York Cavalry. The next idea is the historical significance of that service. "In doing so" is the transition that links the action to the result.

questions.passage: The lack of accessible written sources is a common challenge faced by biographers of pre-nineteenth-century subjects. ______ when writing his biography of Alexander Hamilton (1755–1804), historian Ron Chernow had at his disposal Harold Syrett’s 26-volume, 19,000-document Papers of Alexander Hamilton.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To take one well-known example,

choices.label: B
choices.text: In accordance with this premise,

choices.label: C
choices.text: It thus came as no surprise that,

choices.label: D
choices.text: On the other end of the spectrum,

explanation.key_evidence: The first sentence says many biographers lack accessible written sources, while Chernow had a 26-volume, 19,000-document collection for Hamilton.
explanation.why_correct: Chernow’s situation contrasts sharply with the common challenge described in the first sentence. "On the other end of the spectrum" signals that contrast between scarce sources and unusually abundant sources.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. Chernow is not an example of the common lack of sources; his case is the opposite.

questions.passage: As observed in a 2011 study by Emilio García-Robledo and Alfonso Corzo, macroalgal proliferation may have a suppressive effect on the abundance of cyanobacteria and other microphytobenthos (MPB)—chlorophyll-producing microbes inhabiting marine sediment—in part by reducing the amount of sunlight available to MPB. Examining benthic chlorophyll concentrations (a widely used proxy for MPB biomass) in mudflats in Curlew Bay and other coastal sites in Virginia, Alice F. Besterman and Michael L. Pace found that those concentrations did not negatively correlate with macroalgal proliferation. However, they noted that MPB may respond to low-light conditions by producing higher-than-normal concentrations of chlorophyll, and they thus concluded that ____
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: researchers ought to account for the possibility that because MPB have the capacity to compensate for reduced sunlight availability, benthic chlorophyll concentrations may not always be a reliable indicator of MPB biomass.

choices.label: B
choices.text: although their finding was inconsistent with that of García-Robledo and Corzo, this discrepancy was not attributable to the ability of MPB to accelerate chlorophyll production to mitigate the negative impact of macroalgal accumulations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: although elevated levels of macroalgae do not always correspond to increased levels of benthic chlorophyll, there is likely a larger trend in MPB biomass that is related to macroalgal presence but unrelated to light conditions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the effect of macroalgal concentrations on MPB abundance that García-Robledo and Corzo reported was not observed in Curlew Bay and other Virginia sites because low-light conditions likely are not generalizable across the sites in the studies.

explanation.key_evidence: Besterman and Pace noted that MPB may respond to low-light conditions by producing higher-than-normal chlorophyll concentrations.
explanation.why_correct: Because chlorophyll concentration can increase as a response to low light, it may not reliably track MPB biomass. Thus researchers should account for the possibility that benthic chlorophyll is not always a reliable biomass indicator.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. It follows from the warning that MPB can compensate for low light by producing more chlorophyll.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. The passage says the compensation possibility helps explain why chlorophyll may not show a negative correlation, not that it is irrelevant.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. It speculates about a larger trend unrelated to sunlight, which is not supported.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. The passage does not conclude that low-light effects are not generalizable; it questions chlorophyll concentration as a proxy.

explanation.short: If MPB can produce extra chlorophyll under low light, chlorophyll concentration may not always reliably indicate biomass.
explanation.detailed: The earlier study suggested macroalgae may suppress MPB partly by reducing sunlight. Besterman and Pace did not find a negative correlation using chlorophyll as a proxy for MPB biomass, but they noted that MPB can produce more chlorophyll in low light. That means chlorophyll concentration can mask biomass changes, making choice A the best conclusion.

questions.passage: Neuroscientist Artin Arshamian and his team sought to determine what affects a person’s perception of an odor as pleasant: is it culture, personal taste, or aspects of human anatomy? The team assessed odor preferences in ten groups of people with different modes of living (urban, agricultural, and hunter-gatherer) including the Maniq people from a small community in Thailand and the Seri people from a small community in Mexico. The team observed that across cultures, people generally rated odors about the same: ethyl butyrate, which smells like peaches, was typically rated more pleasant than diethyl disulfide, which smells like garlic. The team’s study thus undermined the idea that _______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: a person who perceives certain odors as pleasant will likely perceive the odors as roughly equal in pleasantness.

choices.label: B
choices.text: culture significantly influences whether a person perceives an odor as pleasant or unpleasant.

choices.label: C
choices.text: personal taste has little influence on whether odors are perceived as pleasant or unpleasant.

choices.label: D
choices.text: people agree in their perception of odors as pleasant or unpleasant regardless of where they live.

explanation.key_evidence: Across ten culturally different groups, people generally rated odors about the same.
explanation.why_correct: If people across cultures generally share odor preferences, the study undermines the idea that culture significantly determines whether odors are perceived as pleasant or unpleasant.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. The study compares different odors across people, not whether one person rates pleasant odors as equally pleasant.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. Similar ratings across cultures weaken the claim that culture significantly shapes odor pleasantness.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. The passage does not show that personal taste has little influence; it focuses on culture.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. This restates the study’s finding rather than the idea that the finding undermines.

explanation.short: The cross-cultural similarity in odor ratings undermines the idea that culture significantly shapes odor pleasantness.
explanation.detailed: The researchers tested groups with different modes of living and found that people generally rated odors similarly across cultures. That result weakens the idea that culture is a major driver of whether people find an odor pleasant or unpleasant.

questions.passage: Many studies have found a positive association between levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury in bodies of fresh water undisturbed by human activity. But Stéphane Guédron, Delphine Tisserand, and colleagues did not find this correlation in an examination of freshwater bodies impacted by wastewater, leading some scientists to hypothesize that the association could be particular to undisturbed waters. However, Ida Tjerngren and colleagues carried out a study on freshwater bodies disturbed by urban development that showed similar results to the studies on undisturbed waters, suggesting that _______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury are both much higher in bodies of fresh water impacted by wastewater than they are in bodies of fresh water disturbed by urban development.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Guédron, Tisserand, and colleagues' study used different methods to measure the concentration of mercury in fresh water than Tjerngren and colleagues' study did.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the effects of wastewater on the association between levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury should not be taken as indicative of the effects of every type of human disturbance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: disturbances linked to wastewater affect significantly more bodies of fresh water than disturbances linked to urban development do.

explanation.key_evidence: Tjerngren and colleagues found in urban-development-disturbed waters the same dissolved organic carbon/mercury association seen in undisturbed waters.
explanation.why_correct: Since urban disturbance did not eliminate the association, the wastewater result should not be generalized to every kind of human disturbance.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. The passage does not compare absolute levels of carbon and mercury in wastewater versus urban-development waters.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. Different measurement methods are not discussed.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. The urban-development study shows that wastewater effects are not representative of all human disturbances.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. The passage does not compare how widespread wastewater and urban-development disturbances are.

explanation.short: The wastewater finding should not be treated as representative of all human disturbances.
explanation.detailed: Some scientists hypothesized that the carbon-mercury association might be limited to undisturbed waters because it was absent in wastewater-impacted waters. But Tjerngren and colleagues found a similar association in waters disturbed by urban development. This suggests wastewater disturbance should not stand in for every type of human disturbance.

questions.passage: Branching in Jurisprudential Schools is one of the hundreds of thousands of manuscripts that have survived from roughly the sixteenth century to the present ____ being passed down through private libraries in the city of Timbuktu, Mali. Many of these manuscripts can be found at the Al-Wangari Manuscript Library.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: day by

choices.label: B
choices.text: day; by

choices.label: C
choices.text: day. By

choices.label: D
choices.text: day by,

explanation.key_evidence: The manuscripts survived from the sixteenth century to the present day by being passed down through private libraries.
explanation.why_correct: The phrase "by being passed down" explains how the manuscripts survived. No punctuation should separate "day" from "by" because the prepositional phrase is essential to the sentence’s meaning.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. "Present day by being passed down" forms a smooth phrase explaining how the manuscripts survived.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. A semicolon would incorrectly separate an incomplete phrase from the explanation.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. A period would make "By being passed down..." a fragment.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. A comma after "by" incorrectly splits the prepositional phrase.

explanation.short: The manuscripts survived to the present day by being passed down through private libraries.
explanation.detailed: The sentence needs the phrase "by being passed down through private libraries" to explain how the manuscripts survived. Choice A keeps this essential phrase connected to "present day" without unnecessary punctuation.

questions.passage: Following the formation of the European Union (EU) that same year, the organizers of the 1992 Tour de France wanted the bike race to reflect the cross-national flow of people and trade that the EU had made possible. The resulting course was 2,500 miles long _____ seven separate borders of neighboring countries, modeled a vision of the EU's unifying aims.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: and, crossed

choices.label: B
choices.text: and had crossed

choices.label: C
choices.text: and crossed

choices.label: D
choices.text: and, crossing

explanation.short: And joins was with modeled; crossing seven borders is a comma-enclosed participial phrase.
explanation.key_evidence: The sentence ends 'modeled a vision of the EU's unifying aims,' providing a finite verb after the blank.
explanation.why_correct: D leaves the complete structure 'The resulting course was ... and modeled ...' and inserts crossing seven borders as a supplementary phrase before modeled.
explanation.detailed: Account for the entire sentence, including the verb after neighboring countries. Removing the intervening description yields 'The resulting course was 2,500 miles long and modeled a vision.' The two commas enclose 'crossing seven separate borders of neighboring countries.' Crossed would introduce another finite predicate but leave modeled without the conjunction it needs.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. Crossed is finite, so it cannot form the parenthetical participial description before modeled.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. Had crossed creates an additional finite predicate, leaving the following modeled uncoordinated.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. Was ... and crossed ... followed by comma modeled does not properly coordinate all three predicates.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. Crossing forms the inserted participial phrase, while and links the finite verbs was and modeled.

questions.passage: As part of his I GOT UP series, Japanese conceptual artist On Kawara spent over a decade—with near daily consistency—mailing postcards to friends declaring what time he got up each day, resulting in pieces such as I Got Up at 7.19 A.M., Jun 6 1977. Such meticulous documentation of mundane ______ artworks that “resonate with existential, psychological and scientific implications about the time-space continuum,” according to the New York Times, became Kawara’s life’s work.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: information, has generated

choices.label: B
choices.text: information generates

choices.label: C
choices.text: information, generating

choices.label: D
choices.text: information generated

explanation.short: Generating artworks adds a description without displacing became as the main verb.
explanation.key_evidence: The core sentence is 'Such meticulous documentation ... became Kawara's life's work.'
explanation.why_correct: C uses generating as a nonfinite participle modifying documentation, preserving the main clause with became as its finite verb.
explanation.detailed: The quotation and the long description separate the subject documentation from became. The blank must therefore introduce a modifier, not a new finite predicate. Generating explains the artworks produced by the documentation and fits inside the existing comma pair.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. Has generated adds an uncoordinated finite verb and is also separated from its subject by a comma.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. Generates introduces an extra finite predicate before became.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. Generating forms a supplementary participial phrase describing the documentation.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. Generated would be a finite verb taking artworks as its object, leaving the later became without coordination.

explanation.why_correct: Choice D uses commas to set off the appositive phrase "a decision that..." after "protest" and to set off the interrupting "by allowing..." phrase.

questions.passage: At a time when many women writers used male pseudonyms to gain greater freedom of self-expression by evading gender conventions, Katherine Bradley and Edith Cooper adapted the practice by publishing poetry, prose, and drama for four decades under the shared name Michael Field. ______ the duo was able to express the joint creative vision that sustained their long personal and professional partnership.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In this way,

choices.label: B
choices.text: For instance,

choices.label: C
choices.text: Later,

choices.label: D
choices.text: On the other hand,

explanation.key_evidence: Bradley and Cooper published under the shared name Michael Field, which let the duo express a joint creative vision.
explanation.why_correct: "In this way" logically connects the method just described—using a shared pseudonym—to the result that followed from that method.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. It shows that publishing under the shared name enabled the joint creative expression described next.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. "For instance" would introduce an example, but the second sentence states a result.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. "Later" suggests a time sequence, not a method-result relationship.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. "On the other hand" signals contrast, but the ideas are complementary.

explanation.short: "In this way" connects the shared pseudonym to the result it enabled.
explanation.detailed: The first sentence explains that Bradley and Cooper adapted the pseudonym practice by writing under the shared name Michael Field. The next sentence explains what that practice allowed them to do. "In this way" is the transition that shows the result came from the method.

questions.passage: In a 2005 study by Mellado et al., the researchers’ aim was to analyze the diet composition of cattle in Coahuila, Mexico. ______ they aimed to analyze the ratio of three different plant subtypes within these animals’ diet: graminoids, forbs, and browse.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Instead,

choices.label: B
choices.text: All the same,

choices.label: C
choices.text: Therefore,

choices.label: D
choices.text: Specifically,

explanation.key_evidence: The second sentence narrows the study aim from cattle diet composition to the ratio of graminoids, forbs, and browse.
explanation.why_correct: "Specifically" introduces a more precise version of the general aim stated in the first sentence.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. "Instead" would indicate a replacement or contrast, but the second sentence specifies the same aim.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. "All the same" signals concession, which is not the relationship here.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. "Therefore" signals a result, but the second sentence is not a consequence.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. "Specifically" introduces the detailed focus within the broader study aim.

explanation.short: "Specifically" narrows the general aim to the exact plant-subtype ratio the researchers studied.
explanation.detailed: The first sentence broadly says the researchers wanted to analyze cattle diet composition. The second sentence gives the specific components they analyzed: graminoids, forbs, and browse. Choice D best signals that narrowing.

questions.passage: John Quincy Adams employed the pseudonym “Marcellus”—a reference to a leader of an ancient Roman army—in political essays he wrote in 1793, a choice that accomplished far more than simply concealing his authorship. _____ it wasn’t an arbitrary pen name but rather a complex rhetorical strategy through which Adams aligned his political views with the venerated republican ideals of the ancient world, thereby bolstering the authority of his writing.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conversely,

choices.label: B
choices.text: In addition,

choices.label: C
choices.text: However,

choices.label: D
choices.text: Indeed,

explanation.key_evidence: The first sentence says the pseudonym did more than conceal authorship; the second explains that it was a complex rhetorical strategy.
explanation.why_correct: "Indeed" reinforces and elaborates on the previous claim by showing exactly how the pseudonym had deeper significance.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. "Conversely" signals contrast, but the second sentence supports the first.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. "In addition" would add a separate point, but the second sentence intensifies the same point.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. "However" signals contrast, which is not present.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. "Indeed" emphasizes and elaborates on the claim that the pseudonym did more than hide authorship.

explanation.short: "Indeed" reinforces the claim that the pseudonym had a deeper rhetorical purpose.
explanation.detailed: The first sentence states that Adams’s pseudonym accomplished more than concealing authorship. The second sentence confirms and expands that idea by explaining that the name aligned his views with ancient republican ideals. "Indeed" is the best transition.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Kale is a vegetable that contains ascorbic acid, an essential nutrient for humans.
• Apricots are fruits that contain ascorbic acid.
• There is 120 milligrams (mg) of ascorbic acid per every 100 grams (g) of kale.
• There is 10 mg of ascorbic acid per every 100 g of apricot.
• Humans cannot make ascorbic acid in their bodies, so they must get it from foods, including fruits and vegetables.
• Ascorbic acid is also known as vitamin C.
questions.prompt: The student wants to refute a claim that apricots are a better source of vitamin C than kale is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Kale contains vitamin C (also known as ascorbic acid); in fact, there is 120 mg of vitamin C in every 100 g of kale.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Kale contains ascorbic acid (also known as vitamin C), and apricots do too.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Humans cannot make ascorbic acid in their bodies, but they can get it from kale and apricots.

choices.label: D
choices.text: With 120 mg of vitamin C per every 100 g, kale is actually a better source of vitamin C than apricots, which contain only 10 mg per every 100 g.

explanation.key_evidence: The notes say kale has 120 mg of vitamin C per 100 g, while apricots have only 10 mg per 100 g.
explanation.why_correct: To refute the claim that apricots are better, the answer must directly compare the vitamin C amounts and show that kale has more. Choice D does this.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. It gives kale’s vitamin C amount but does not compare it with apricots.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. It says both contain vitamin C, but that does not refute the claim that apricots are better.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. It explains why humans need food sources of vitamin C but does not compare kale and apricots.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. It directly refutes the claim by showing kale has much more vitamin C per 100 g than apricots.

explanation.short: Choice D refutes the claim by comparing the amounts: kale has 120 mg per 100 g, while apricots have 10 mg.
explanation.detailed: The goal is to refute a claim that apricots are the better vitamin C source. The relevant evidence is the direct numerical comparison: kale contains 120 mg per 100 g, while apricots contain 10 mg per 100 g. Choice D uses that comparison to show kale is actually better.
